reasons: No test is visible for this file.
Every quote and row name must match the report text exactly, so small report edits will stop the import.
The Samson check depends on a saved copy of a web page.

terms.meaning: A short code calculated from a file's contents. If even one character changes, the code changes.
A shared rule check that a project record has the right shape and allowed values.
Add missing information to an existing record without changing what is already stored.
Where a project is in its life, such as under construction or operating.
An exact piece of source text stored as proof for a fact about a project.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loading the report and locating the project root
sections.what: Reads the uploaded solar report from disk and works out where the project root is. Nothing is shown to users directly, but the rest of the import has no text to check quotes against without this step.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the fact that every later check uses the report text.
sections.watch_out: The report path is fixed in the code, so renaming or moving the report file breaks the import.

sections.name: reportHash, clean, cells
sections.title: Report fingerprint and text cleaning helpers
sections.what: Calculates a fingerprint of the report so every change record can say which exact version was imported. It also holds small helpers that strip citation markers and bold marks and split table rows into cells.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fingerprint lets an audit trail prove which report version a change came from.
sections.watch_out: The citation cleanup removes every occurrence of the letters cite, even inside ordinary words such as excite, so report text can be altered.

sections.name: table, Source, Participant, Milestone
sections.title: Reading report tables and source register
sections.what: Finds named sections of the report, reads their tables, and builds the source register. Each source gets a link, a publisher name, a date and a quote. The file also defines the shapes used for participants and milestones.
sections.why: Reading tables by section heading and row name, not by row order, is stated in the comment on the entries list.
sections.watch_out: A missing section heading or a source row with no link stops the whole file from loading.

sections.name: Entry, p, m
sections.title: Shape of a hand-entered project
sections.what: Defines everything one reviewed project must contain, such as its name, country, aliases, lifecycle stage, capacity, storage, cost, participants and milestones. Two small helpers make participant and milestone entries short to write.
sections.why: A single shape means every reviewed project is processed the same way.
sections.watch_out: Many optional fields such as stage, capacity and operator are missing in some entries, so code that reads them must allow for empty values.

sections.name: entries (part 1)
sections.title: Reviewed solar projects, first group
sections.what: The hand-checked list of the first group of solar projects, from the Abu Dhabi project through Antelope Valley. Each entry gives its name, country, sources, stage, costs, owners and dates. Some entries note that a date is only a month or a year, or that a figure is a forecast rather than actual spending.
sections.why: The comment above the list says these were reviewed together, and that table positions are never used to match them.
sections.watch_out: The stage and cost wording here is what users read. Changing a stage is a reviewed decision, not a typo fix.

sections.name: entries (part 2)
sections.title: Reviewed solar projects, second group
sections.what: Continues the list with the remaining projects, Antelope Valley One and Mammoth Solar, in the same structure. The Mammoth entry notes that its cost figures are not audited actual spending.
sections.why: Same reason as the first group: each project is reviewed by hand.
sections.watch_out: A new project must use source IDs that exist in the register, or the import will fail when that entry runs.

sections.name: namedRow
sections.title: Finding exactly one named table row
sections.what: Looks up a table row by its project name, after cleaning, and insists there is exactly one match. It also holds the provenance statement that says the quotes come from the uploaded report and were not checked live.
sections.why: Requiring exactly one match is the explicit way to avoid picking the wrong row.
sections.watch_out: Names must match exactly after cleaning, so renaming a row in the report stops the import with an error.

sections.name: prepare
sections.title: Preparing one project's record
sections.what: Builds a project's record from its report rows, including description, report attributes, capacity, cost, schedule and participants, along with the stage and status text. It then runs the record through the shared renewables checks. Both the planning and evidence steps use this.
sections.why: Reason for the shared check not stated in the code beyond the function's use by both steps.
sections.watch_out: If a stage is already stored for the project, that stored stage is used instead of the reviewed one, so the two can differ.

sections.name: reportEvidence
sections.title: Collecting evidence quotes for a project
sections.what: Builds the list of evidence quotes for one project. Every quote must be an exact piece of the uploaded report, or the function stops. It also adds a quote from a saved copy of the Samson source page and attaches register quotes to their sources. Topaz and Agua Caliente share one register row, so the code keeps each project's cost quote separate.
sections.why: The comment says one register row covers two projects, so one project's quote must not be attached to the other.
sections.watch_out: The Samson check reads a saved page. If that file changes or is missing, the import fails for that project.

sections.name: reportLine
sections.title: Finding the report line of a quote
sections.what: Returns the line number in the report where a quote appears, so change records can point a reviewer to the exact place.
sections.why: Likely reason: traceability, so a reviewer can check a fact against the report quickly.
sections.watch_out: If a quote is not found on any single line, the function returns 0, which looks like a real line number.

summary: Holds the hand-reviewed list of solar projects from one uploaded research report and turns each one into a planned import record with its sources, participants, milestones and evidence quotes.
purpose: Provides the reviewed facts for the solar report import, so the importer uses names and scopes that a person checked and never relies on table position.
why: Likely reason: the report's tables are messy, so the project list is written out by hand and each quote is checked against the report text. The code says explicitly that entries are never matched by position.
how: First, the report file is read and fingerprinted. Its tables are split by section heading. A source register is read from one table. Each project is then defined by hand, pointing to its table rows and source IDs. When a project is prepared, its record is checked against the shared renewables rules. Finally, evidence quotes are collected and each one must match the report text exactly, or the run stops.
inputs: The uploaded solar report file under attached_assets, the saved source page for the Samson project under artifacts/api-server/data/solar-report, and the hand-written project list in this file.
outputs: The project entries, the source register, the function that prepares one project record, the function that lists evidence quotes for a project, the line-finding function, the provenance statement, and the report fingerprint.
risks: Almost every check depends on the report's exact wording. Editing the report changes its fingerprint and can make named rows or quotes fail. The Samson check reads a saved file, so it fails if that file changes or goes missing. A hand-written entry that names a source ID not in the register will fail when that entry runs.
debug: If the error says Expected one named row, check that the row name in the report matches the capacity or detail row name in the entry. If it says Quote missing from report, the report text has changed since the quote was written. If it says the Samson construction-stage excerpt no longer matches, the saved page in the data folder no longer contains the quoted sentence. If a source is undefined, check the entry's source IDs.
